content.text: How to watch the New York Yankees without cable in 2026 As the 2026 MLB season gets underway, New York Yankees fans have more ways than ever to catch every pitch, clutch hit, and late-inning drama — without a traditional cable subscription. Whether you're following the Yankees through Spring Training, the regular season, or into an October postseason run, this guide lays out exactly how to stream every New York Yankees game in 2026, including the best services, platform recommendations, and key scheduling tips. Subscribe to Fubo to stream New York Yankees games all season long: Start with a free trial! Why Fubo Is the Best Choice for Yankees Fans Fubo is one of only two live-TV streaming platforms that carries YES Network (the Yankees Entertainment and Sports Network) — the exclusive regional home of Yankees baseball in the New York market. In 2024, Fubo and YES Network inked a multi-year deal ensuring the network remains available on the platform for the foreseeable future for subscribers within the YES Network regional footprint, which covers all of New York State and Connecticut, along with northern and central New Jersey and parts of northeastern Pennsylvania. About YES Network YES Network — the Yankees Entertainment and Sports Network — has been the home of Yankees baseball since 2002, and 2026 marks the network's 25th anniversary season. The broadcast booth has been overhauled for the new season, with YES trimming its roster of voices down to a focused, familiar core. Michael Kay returns as the lead play-by-play voice, entering his 35th year broadcasting Yankees baseball and his 25th on YES — a multi-Emmy Award winner whose voice is synonymous with Yankee Stadium itself. Ryan Ruocco serves as Kay's backup, handling approximately 15 games while balancing duties with ESPN. The analyst rotation features three Yankees legends: David Cone, a World Series hero and one of baseball's sharpest pitching minds; Paul O'Neill, a five-time World Series champion in his 25th season with the network; and Joe Girardi, the former Yankees manager and two-time World Series winner who steps in when needed. Meredith Marakovits continues in her longtime field reporter role, providing in-game coverage and the insider access Yankees fans have come to rely on. YES airs the vast majority of New York's games not claimed by national broadcast windows, making it the centerpiece of any Yankees streaming setup. What About Out-of-Market Yankees Fans? If you live outside the YES Network's regional footprint and can't access it locally, Fubo still has you covered. MLB.TV is available as an add-on through Fubo, letting you stream every out-of-market regular season game live and on demand. This is the gold standard for fans following their team from afar, giving you access to all 162 games regardless of where you live. Note that standard MLB.TV blackout restrictions apply: if you're within the YES Network's home market, those games will be blacked out on MLB.TV (which is why YES Network via Fubo is the right solution for local fans). The 2026 Yankees: A Team Built to Win The Yankees enter 2026 with championship hunger after a 94-68 season in 2025 — their second consecutive year with that record — that ended in an ALDS loss to the Toronto Blue Jays. New York is chasing its 28th World Series title and its first since 2009, and all indications point to a team with the depth and star power to make a deep run. The lineup is anchored by reigning three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge, who had a historic 2025 — leading the major leagues in batting average (.331), on-base percentage (.457), and slugging percentage (.688) while setting career highs in multiple categories. Judge is surrounded by a formidable supporting cast: Jazz Chisholm Jr., who joined the 30/30 club with 31 home runs and 31 stolen bases in 2025; Cody Bellinger, re-signed to anchor the outfield; Giancarlo Stanton returning healthy at DH; and slick-fielding third baseman Ryan McMahon, acquired at the 2025 trade deadline and now in his first full season in the Bronx. First baseman Ben Rice is poised for a breakout, and veterans Paul Goldschmidt and Amed Rosario add valuable depth. On the mound, the story of the 2026 season will be the phased return of the rotation's two biggest arms. Gerrit Cole, the Yankees' ace, missed all of 2025 following Tommy John surgery and is targeting a return in May or June — a reinforcement that could be as impactful as any offseason signing. Carlos Rodón is also working his way back and expected to return in April or May, eventually giving New York one of the deepest rotations in baseball. Until then, the staff is led by Max Fried, who went 19-5 with a 2.86 ERA in his first Yankees season, joined by rising arms Cam Schlittler, Will Warren, and newly acquired lefty Ryan Weathers, traded from Miami with breakout potential. The bullpen is anchored by closer David Bednar (acquired at last year's deadline) alongside Camilo Doval, who gives manager Aaron Boone two elite late-inning options. With the deepest lineup in the AL East, reinforcements arriving midseason, and an iconic postseason pedigree, the 2026 Yankees are very much in the hunt for championship No. 28. 2026 New York Yankees Season: Key Dates to Know Spring Training Begins: February 20, 2026 Regular Season Opener: March 25, 2026 (at San Francisco Giants) Jackie Robinson Day: April 15, 2026 All-Star Week: July 11–14, 2026 Home Run Derby: July 13, 2026 Trade Deadline: August 3, 2026 MLB at Field of Dreams: August 13, 2026 Postseason Begins: September 29, 2026 World Series: October 23, 2026 Tips for Streaming the Yankees Like a Pro Start with Fubo as your base — it's one of only two streaming services that carry YES Network, making it essential for in-market Yankees fans across New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, and northeastern Pennsylvania. Add MLB.TV as an add-on through Fubo for out-of-market coverage — this gives you every regular season game live and on demand, perfect if you're outside the YES Network footprint. Add the Sports Plus package for MLB Network — daily baseball programming and select live games make it a worthwhile upgrade for the serious fan. Set up Cloud DVR for doubleheaders and late games — Fubo's Unlimited Cloud DVR lets you record games so you never miss an inning, even on busy nights with overlapping matchups. Check national windows early — the Yankees are one of the most frequently featured teams on FOX Saturday baseball and ESPN weeknight games; these are already included in your Fubo package. Monitor the playoff broadcast schedule in September — postseason rights shift each round, so check which networks have each series and confirm your Fubo plan covers them. How to Stream Every Yankees Game in 2026: The Bottom Line For Yankees fans, the path to streaming every game in 2026 is straightforward: Subscribe to Fubo for YES Network (local games), FOX/FS1, ESPN/ESPN2/ABC, and ESPN+ — covering the backbone of the Yankees broadcast schedule. Add MLB.TV as an add-on through Fubo for every out-of-market regular season game live and on demand. Add Sports Plus for MLB Network access and additional live game coverage. Use Fubo's Unlimited Cloud DVR to record any game you can't watch live. With this setup — and a quick check of your local market and blackout rules — you'll be ready to stream every pitch of the 2026 New York Yankees season.
